history.content: Hi There! Why the Berlin wall was called Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart ?

The Berlin Wall was officially referred to as the 'Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart' by the GDR (East German) authorities. This name implied an equivalence between NATO countries, including West Germany, and fascists. However, this justification was met with skepticism by many, as the Wall primarily seemed to serve the purpose of preventing the citizens of East Germany from entering or fleeing to West Berlin. The West Berlin city government sometimes referred to it as the "Wall of Shame'', a term coined by mayor Willy Brandt in reference to the Wall's restriction on freedom of movement.  It came to symbolize physically the "Iron Curtain'' that separated Western Europe and the Eastern Bloc during the Cold War.
What was the real reason to have a wall dividing Germany?

The real reason for the construction of the Berlin Wall was to prevent the massive emigration and defection that had been occurring from East Germany and the communist Eastern Bloc during the post-World War II period. The East German government portrayed the Wall as protecting its population from fascist elements conspiring to prevent the 'will of the people' in building a socialist state in East Germany. The construction of the Wall had caused considerable hardship to families divided by it.
How long did it take to build the wall and how long was it?

The construction of the Berlin Wall began on 13 August 1961 and it was more than 140 kilometers (87 mi) long. In June 1962, a second, parallel fence was built some 100 meters (110 yd) farther into East German territory, which established what later became known as the 'death strip'.
I can imagine how many people died to cross it.

Yes, the exact number of people who died trying to cross the Berlin Wall is disputed, but it is generally accepted to be at least 140, according to a historic research group at the Center for Contemporary Historical Research (ZZF) in Potsdam. The most vocal claims by Alexandra Hildebrandt, Director of the Checkpoint Charlie Museum and widow of the Museum's founder, estimated the death toll to be well above 200. During the years of the Wall, around 5,000 people successfully defected to West Berlin from the  100,000 people that attempted to escape. The first person to be shot and killed while trying to cross to West Berlin was Günter Litfin , a twenty - four - year - old tailor . He attempted to swim across the Spree Canal to West Germany on 24 August 1961 , the same day that East German police had received shoot - to - kill orders to prevent anyone from escaping  and e last person to be shot and killed while trying to cross the border was Chris Gueffroy on 6 February 1989 , while the final person to die in an escape attempt was Winfried Freudenberg who was killed when his homemade natural gas - filled balloon crashed on 8 March 1989.
What terrible time for the Germans.
Yes, indeed.   Do you have any additional questions?
